at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.11.2026) The Commission shares the objective of translating European defence spending into common European capabilities, greater interoperability and less fragmentation. Defence planning remains the responsibility of Member States, yet the Commission supports cooperation across the life cycle of defence products, from research and development to production and common procurement, fostering coherence between EU funding and national investments. Under the 2028-2034 Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF), the Commission has proposed the European Competitiveness Fund (ECF)1 to foster innovation and competitiveness in critical sectors – such as defence and security – through dedicated collaborate actions, like European Defence Projects of Common Interest. The security of supply regime under the European Defence Industry Programme (EDIP)2 will help identify bottlenecks and areas for joint action. Progress is tracked in the Annual Defence Readiness Report, first presented to the 15-16 October 2026 European Council. The Commission has also proposed EUR 17.6 billion for military mobility under the Connecting Europe Facility (CEF), in the next MFF. In addition, the ECF will support access to key transport and logistical capabilities, protection and development of cross-border critical military mobility infrastructure, efforts to increase threat awareness and resilience, and investments in strategic sectors – complemented by regulatory measures under the proposed Military Mobility Regulation3.
